# Touchy-Pad

> Touchy-Pad is an open-source firmware + host SDK that turns cheap ($15–30)
> ESP32 boards into **host-driven displays**: multitouch LCD touchpads,
> StreamDeck-style macro keypads, and LED-matrix art panels. The device is a
> *dumb renderer* — your host program (Python or Rust) authors a protobuf widget
> tree, uploads it over USB / UART / WiFi-HTTP, and the device renders it with
> LVGL and reports touches back. Macros and gestures compile into on-device
> `Action` lists, so a keypad keeps working with no host process attached.

Read this file first, then follow the links in the last section for depth. It is
written for an AI coding agent that wants to *make something* with Touchy-Pad:
author screens, drive LCD or LED panels, stream live updates, bind gestures.

## Facts you must know before writing code

- **Two supported host APIs.** Python: the `touchy_pad.api` package (PyPI
  `touchy-pad`). Rust: the async `touchy-pad` crate in `rust/touchy-pad/`.
  Everything else (`touchy_pad._proto`, `sim/`, `cli.py`) is internal.
- **One protocol, every transport.** Self-synchronising frames
  `MAGIC(0xA5 0x5A) | LEN(u16 LE) | payload | CRC8` over USB vendor bulk,
  USB-CDC-ACM, hardware UART, or TCP (the simulator). The *same* `Command` /
  `Response` messages also ride a bare (unframed) protobuf **or JSON** HTTP(S)
  endpoint, so `curl` can drive a panel too.
- **Screens are protobuf, not XML/HTML.** Widgets are LVGL objects described by
  `proto/widgets.proto`. The device is layout-agnostic: it materialises whatever
  tree you send.
- **Wire versions at HEAD:** `Widget.Version.CURRENT == 30`,
  `SysBoardInfoResponse.ProtocolVersion.CURRENT == 14`,
  `PreferencesFile.Version.CURRENT == 9`. The version lives on the **root
  `Widget`** of every screen/widget file (there is no `Screen.Version`); the
  host DSL stamps it for you — only hand-build it for raw protobuf.
- **The firmware has no unit tests.** Host-side `pytest` (`just app-test`)
  only. Every host feature is developed against the **simulator**, which speaks
  the real wire protocol.
- **You do not need hardware to develop.** `touchy --sim-headless`,
  `touchy --sim-gui`, or a standalone `touchy simulator` + `TOUCHY_SIM_URL`.

## The mental model

```text
your script (Python / Rust)                        $15 ESP32 board
  screens DSL        -> Screen / Widget protobuf  ─USB/UART/HTTP─>  LVGL renders it
  macros + actions   -> Action lists                                user touches it
  ImageCache         -> hashed assets on T:       <───────────────  events + USB HID out
```

- **You author screens; the device stores them.** `pad.screen_save(screen)`
  writes `F:host/s/<name>.pb` (persistent LittleFS). `pad.screen_load(...)`
  activates one.
- **The stock chrome + "user screens" is the usual path.** `F:host/s/default.pb`
  is a prev/next bar plus a body `widget_ref(id="page")`.
  `pad.user_screen_save("demo", widget)` writes `F:host/uscr/demo.pb` and
  `pad.show_user_screen("demo")` points that ref at it — your UI without
  replacing the chrome.
- **Behaviour lives on the device.** `macro_action([...])` becomes a device-side
  HID sequence (keyboard / mouse / consumer keys) that works with no host
  running. `host_action(on_event=cb)` instead sends an event back to your
  process. Both are just `Action` lists attached to a widget.
- **The host can mutate a live screen** without re-uploading it:
  `pad.set_properties([...])` applies sticky, session-scoped LVGL property
  overrides (text, colour, geometry, `anim_duration`, …) in one RPC, and counts
  as display activity (it wakes / keeps awake the backlight).
- **Drive-prefixed paths everywhere:** `F:` persistent flash (LittleFS),
  `R:` volatile PSRAM ramdisk, `T:` transient drive (PSRAM ramdisk, or flash
  scratch on no-PSRAM boards). Screens `F:host/s/`, user pages `F:host/uscr/`,
  standalone widgets `F:host/w/`, images wherever you like.

## Install and connect (Python)

```sh
pip install touchy-pad          # host library + the `touchy` CLI
pip install 'touchy-pad[sim]'   # + PySide6 simulator window
touchy update                   # flash the right firmware onto a connected board
touchy init                     # provision chrome + a trackpad page on a fresh device
```

```python
from touchy_pad.api import touchy_open, touchy_get_pad_ids

print("attached:", touchy_get_pad_ids())        # stable serials, e.g. ["t0a1b2c3d4e5f"]

with touchy_open() as pad:                      # serial= to pick a specific device
    info = pad.board_info                       # a SysBoardInfoResponse
    print(info.board_name,                      # "jc4827w543", "esp32_s3_matrix", "sim", …
          info.display_width, info.display_height,
          "touch:", info.is_touchable, "multitouch:", info.is_multitouch,
          "usb:", info.has_usb, "serial:", info.serial)
```

`touchy_open(serial=None, *, url=None)` resolution order: `url=` / `TOUCHY_URL`
(HTTP(S) endpoint) → native USB → `uart:<path>` serial bridge → `TOUCHY_SIM_URL`
simulator → in-process simulator. It raises `IncompatibleFirmwareError` when the
device firmware is older than `MINIMUM_FIRMWARE_VERSION`. `Touchy` is a context
manager: leaving the `with` stops the background event-poller thread and closes
the transport.

Useful `pad.board_info` fields: `board_name`, `display_width`, `display_height`,
`is_touchable` (False on LED-matrix boards — hide touch-only UI),
`is_multitouch`, `has_usb`, `serial`, `protocol_version`,
`firmware_version_str`, `free_heap_bytes`, `free_psram_bytes`,
`fs_total_bytes` / `fs_used_bytes` (LittleFS capacity/usage), `temp_is_flash`
(advisory: `T:` is flash-backed on this board, so throttle high-rate writes).

## Python quickstart — a complete, runnable program

```python
"""Upload a 2x2 page to the device, show it, and react to taps."""
from touchy_pad.api import (
    Layer, grid, cell, label, button,
    style, host_action, macro_action, macros, hid_keys,
    protobuf, touchy_open,
)


def build_page() -> protobuf.Widget:
    """Build one user-screen page body (a single Widget)."""
    page = Layer(layout=grid(cols=2, rows=2, gap=8))

    page += cell(
        label("title", text="Status panel", font_size=24,
              style=style(text_color=0xFFFFFF)),
        col=0, row=0, col_span=2, grow_x=1,
    )
    # Runs on the *device*: emits a real USB keyboard shortcut.
    page += cell(
        button("copy", text="Ctrl+C",
               on_click=macro_action([macros.key_tap(hid_keys.KEY_C, hid_keys.CTRL)])),
        col=0, row=1, grow_x=1,
    )
    # Runs in *this* process: the device sends the event back to us.
    page += cell(
        button("ping", text="Ping host",
               on_click=host_action(on_event=lambda e: print("tapped", e.user_data))),
        col=1, row=1, grow_x=1,
    )

    widget = protobuf.Widget()          # Layer -> Widget (the unit the API uploads)
    page.copy_into(widget)
    return widget


with touchy_open() as pad:
    pad.user_screen_save("panel", build_page())   # -> F:host/uscr/panel.pb
    pad.show_user_screen("panel")                 # bring it to the front
    print("Page is live — tap the device. Ctrl-C to quit.")
    try:
        import time
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
```

Inline `host_action(on_event=...)` callbacks are auto-registered when the screen
or page that references them is uploaded (`screen_save` / `user_screen_save` /
`widget_save`), so no manual wiring is needed. Callbacks run on the poller
thread: keep them short and lock any shared state. A fully commented version of
this program is `app/examples/demo.py`.

## Screen / widget DSL cheat sheet

Almost everything authoring-related is re-exported from `touchy_pad.api` (the
exception is the low-level animation builders — see the Animations row). The DSL
builds protobuf messages; `pad.screen_save()` / `user_screen_save()` /
`widget_save()` upload them.

```python
from touchy_pad.api import *          # every authoring name in the table below
from touchy_pad.api import macros     # (macros is a submodule — import it explicitly)
```

| Area | Names |
|---|---|
| Layouts | `absolute()`, `flex(flow, gap)`, `row(gap)`, `col(gap)`, `grid(cols, rows=0, gap=0)`, `cell(w, col, row, col_span=1, row_span=1, *, grow_x, grow_y)`, `rect(x, y, w, h)`, `grow(w, x=, y=)` |
| Widgets | `button(id, text, on_click, on_press, on_release, …)`, `label(id, text, font_size, text_align, long_mode, recolor, scroll_duration_ms, scroll_speed_px_s, …)`, `slider(id, min, max, value, on_change)`, `toggle(id, on, on_change)`, `checkbox(id, text, checked, on_change)`, `image(id, asset, scale, rotation)`, `image_button(id, asset, pressed_asset, on_click, …, scale, pressed_scale)`, `arc(id, min, max, value)`, `spacer(id)`, `widget_ref(path, *, id)`, `trackpad(id, …)`, `log_line(id)`, `fps(id)`, `force_render(id)` |
| Styling | `style(bg_color, radius, border_w, pad, text_color, font_size, recolor, recolor_opa, transform_width, shadow_width, for_state, transition)` — colours are `0xRRGGBB` ints; `for_state` is an `LvState` bitmask (e.g. `STATE_PRESSED`). Stack several by passing a list. `transition(props, path, duration_ms, delay_ms)` animates a style change. |
| Animations | `ripple_animation(...)` and `AnimPath` are re-exported; `animation(*anim_track(...), duration_ms, path, repeat_count, reverse, …)` and `anim_track(prop, start, end, *, start_inverted, end_inverted)` live in `touchy_pad.api.screens` (`prop` is a `StyleProp` member, e.g. `StyleProp.X`). Pass them via the widget factories' `animations=` argument. |
| Actions | `action(...)`, `host_action(code=None, *, on_event=callable)`, `macro_action(steps)`, `device_action(...)`, `change_widget_ref_action(id, path)`, `next_widget_action(id, dir)` / `prev_widget_action(id, dir)`, `set_image_button_slot_action(id, pressed, path)` |
| Enums / consts | `AnimPath`, `LongMode`, `LvState`, `StyleProp`, `TextAlign`, `SCROLL_SPEED_MIN_PX_S` / `SCROLL_SPEED_MAX_PX_S` |
| Lifecycle | `touchy_open`, `touchy_get_pad_ids`, `Touchy`, `TouchyClient`, `TouchyError`, `IncompatibleFirmwareError`, `ImageCache`, `Color`, `Point`, `build_property_override`, `protobuf` (raw generated classes) |
| Macros | `macros.key_tap/key_down/key_up/type_text`, `macros.mouse_click/mouse_move/scroll_move/zoom_move/mouse_button_down/mouse_button_up`, `macros.consumer_key(VOLUME_UP\|VOLUME_DOWN\|MUTE\|PLAY_PAUSE)`, `macros.set_delay/delay`, `hid_keys.*` (import `macros` explicitly — it is not part of `import *`) |
| Upload helpers | `Screen(name, layout=, widgets=, *, top=, sys=, bottom=)`, `Layer(layout=, widgets=)` (use `Layer` when you want a `widget_ref`-style body without a whole screen), `build_default_screen()`, `build_demo_screen()`, `build_setup_screen_touchless()` |

`Touchy` methods: `screen_save(screen, *, name=None) -> name`,
`screen_load(path)`, `user_screen_save(name, widget, *, drive="F")`,
`widget_save(name, widget, *, drive="F")`, `show_user_screen(name, *, drive="F")`,
`file_save(path, data, *, max_width=None, max_height=None)`, `file_delete(path)`,
`file_reset()`, `set_properties(entries)`, `set_image_button_slot(id, pressed, path)`,
`on_host_event(code, cb)`, `board_info`, `client` (`TouchyClient`).
`TouchyClient` (low level) adds `screen_wake()`, `run_actions(actions)`,
`set_preferences(prefs)`, `get_preferences()`, `set_backlight_level(0..100)`,
`screen_sleep_timeout(ms)`, `set_min_log_level(level)`, `sys_board_info_get()`,
`event_consume()`, `stream_events()`.

## Layout and sizing rules (get these right)

The device sizes widgets exactly like LVGL, with one opt-in twist:

- **Everything is content-sized by default.** A button shrinks to its text. There
  is no implicit stretching — opt in with `grow_x` / `grow_y` (`grow(w, x=1)` or
  `cell(..., grow_x=1)`).
- **Flex main axis** (`x` in a `row`, `y` in a `col`) is an `lv_obj_set_flex_grow`
  *factor* — proportional, so `2` grows twice as fast as `1`.
- **Flex cross axis** (`y` in a `row`, `x` in a `col`) and **grid** (both axes)
  treat any value `> 0` as "fill"; the magnitude is ignored.
- **Grid cells centre by default** (`LV_GRID_ALIGN_CENTER`); use `grow_x`/`grow_y`
  for `STRETCH`. A `grow_x=1` spacer between two buttons pushes them to opposite
  edges.
- **`rect(x, y, w, h)`** only applies under an `absolute()` layout (or as a fixed
  size hint); `w`/`h` of `0` mean "size to content".
- **Scrolling labels need a fixed, narrower width** — set it via `rect` or a
  sizing parent (flex grow / grid stretch). Otherwise `long_mode` never animates.
- Layering: use a `1x1` `grid` and put several widgets in the same `cell(...)` —
  LVGL dispatches touch to the last-drawn (topmost) object. That is how the stock
  trackpad page stacks background / hint / trackpad.
- `Screen` also exposes LVGL's persistent layers: `add_top()` / `add_sys()` /
  `add_bottom()` (widgets there survive screen switches until replaced).

## Actions: on-device behaviour vs. host callbacks

An `Action` list on a widget is what makes it *do* something. Two kinds matter:

```python
from touchy_pad.api import (button, host_action, macro_action, macros, hid_keys,
                            protobuf, change_widget_ref_action)

    # (1) DEVICE-SIDE: emitted as real USB HID by the device itself —
    #     works with no host process attached.
button("paste", text="Paste",
       on_click=macro_action([macros.key_tap(hid_keys.KEY_V, hid_keys.CTRL)]))

    # (2) HOST-SIDE: the device sends an LvEvent; your callable runs here.
button("ping", text="Ping",
       on_click=host_action(on_event=lambda e: print("widget", e.user_data, "fired")))
```

- `host_action(on_event=...)` allocates a unique code from a reserved range
  (`>= 0x10000`) and registers the callable automatically on upload. With an
  explicit code (`host_action(0x100)`, keep it **below** `0x10000`) you must
  dispatch it yourself: `pad.on_host_event(0x100, cb)`.
- `LvEvent` fields: `user_data` (the widget id), `value` (sliders),
  `checked` (toggles/checkboxes), `host_code`, and `code` (`1`=PRESSED,
  `8`=RELEASED, `7`=CLICKED).
- **Any** action list can also be fired from the host right now:
  `pad.client.run_actions([...])` executes it device-side as if a widget had
  triggered it (this is what `show_user_screen()` uses).
- Handy macros: `key_tap/key_down/key_up`, `type_text`, `mouse_click`,
  `mouse_move` (bare call = the trackpad's live per-frame delta),
  `scroll_move`, `zoom_move`, `mouse_button_down/up`, `set_delay`,
  `consumer_key(VOLUME_UP | VOLUME_DOWN | MUTE | PLAY_PAUSE)`. Keys live in
  `hid_keys` (`KEY_*`, `MOD_*`, `CTRL`/`SHIFT`/`ALT` aliases).

## Live updates without re-uploading the screen

```python
from touchy_pad.api import Color, Point, build_property_override

with touchy_open() as pad:
    pad.set_properties([
        build_property_override("welcome", "text", "New message"),   # label text
        build_property_override("box", "bg_color", Color(0xFF8800)), # colour
        build_property_override("box", "x", 12),                     # integer prop
        build_property_override("ticker", "anim_duration", 1000),    # ms per scroll lap
        build_property_override("welcome", "text", None),            # remove override
    ])
```

- `prop` is an **LVGL property name** (`"text"`, `"bg_color"`, `"x"`, `"w"`,
  `"opa"`, `"anim_duration"`, …) or a raw `lv_prop_id_t` int.
- Value type selects the wire payload: `bool` → bool, `int` → int, `str` → text,
  `Color(0xRRGGBB)` → colour, `Point(x, y)` → point, `None` → **remove**.
  `Color`/`Point` wrappers are required — a bare `int` is always an integer prop.
- Overrides are **session-scoped (RAM only) and sticky**: they re-apply whenever
  the target widget is (re)built, and work even if it is not loaded yet. An
  absent widget is not an error; a malformed entry fails the RPC without
  aborting the rest.
- A batch is **one atomic RPC**, repaints immediately, and counts as display
  activity — it wakes / keeps awake the backlight, so animating at a few Hz
  needs no explicit `pad.client.screen_wake()`.
- The simulator honours the subset `x`/`y`/`w`/`h`, `bg_color`, `text`; anything
  else logs a warning and is ignored.

## Images

```python
from touchy_pad.api import ImageCache, ImageSource, image, image_button, touchy_open

with touchy_open() as pad:
    # Upload a PNG/JPEG/BMP/GIF/WebP — auto-converted to LVGL .bin.
    # max_width/max_height downscale (aspect preserved) before conversion.
    pad.file_save("F:host/images/logo.png", png_bytes, max_width=128, max_height=128)
    # -> widget: image("logo", asset="F:host/images/logo.bin")

    cache = ImageCache(pad, max_dim=72)        # one per device, not thread-safe
    path = cache.set_cached_image(icon_png)    # uploads once, returns T:host/icache/<hash>.bin
    again = cache.set_cached_image(icon_png)   # cache hit: no device I/O
    assert path == again

    # Repaint one slot of an on-screen ImageButton in place (no rebuild → the
    # pressed key keeps its touch state and still emits a release).
    pad.set_image_button_slot("key_0", pressed=False, path=path)
```

- **`ImageCache`** is content-addressed (xxh3-128): identical bytes upload once,
  LRU-evicted after 128 entries, stored under `T:host/icache/`. Build a fresh
  cache per attach (the first call wipes the cache root). This is the
  StreamDeck-style repaint path.
- **`ImageSource`** is a *live* asset bound to a stable `T:dyn/<n>.bin` path:
  `src = ImageSource(frame_callable, every=0.2)`, put it in
  `image("w", src)` / `image_button("k", src)`, then `src.update()` (or
  `src.update(new=pil_image)`) re-renders and **rewrites the file, which is the
  repaint** — no action, no screen reload. `start()`/`stop()` drive the `every=`
  background thread. `image()`/`image_button()` also accept a bare
  `PIL.Image` or `bytes` (auto-wrapped).
- A `.gif` keeps its extension and stays animated (`lv_gif` decodes it
  on-device); everything else becomes `.bin`.
- Prefer `R:`/`T:` for assets rewritten often (icons, animation frames) to avoid
  flash wear; `F:` for things that should survive reboot.

## Driving an LED-matrix (touch-less) panel

LED boards (`esp32_s3_matrix`, `esp32_s3_devkitc_1`; `jc_esp32p4_m3` is parked)
have **no touch panel** and, until configured, **no panel at all** — a fresh
board reports `display_width == 0` and renders nothing. Configure it once from
the host:

```sh
touchy pref from-template led-32x8        # 32x8 WS2812B matrix on GPIO 4
touchy pref from-template led-96x8-chain  # 3 x 32x8 daisy-chained, tiled 96x8
touchy pref from-template led-32x32-chain
touchy pref backlight-level 40            # LED boards default to 10 % brightness
touchy board-info                         # now reports the real 32x8 / 96x8 size
```

Templates live in `app/src/touchy_pad/assets/templates/*.json`; they install a
whole `PreferencesFile`, including `board_config` — a chain of up to **4**
daisy-chained panels on one data GPIO, tiled into one logical surface
(`tile_by_row=false` → horizontal). Each panel carries wiring flags
(`rows_snaked` / `cols_snaked` — both default **true** — plus `row_major`,
`cols_flipped`, `rows_flipped`); edit the JSON and `touchy pref json-set` it, or
`touchy pref json-get` to read the live config back.

```python
from touchy_pad.api import absolute, rect, label, StyleProp, Screen, touchy_open
from touchy_pad.api.screens import animation, anim_track   # not re-exported from .api

with touchy_open() as pad:
    info = pad.board_info
    if not info.is_touchable:                       # an LED matrix, not an LCD
        w, h = info.display_width, info.display_height
        s = Screen("matrix", layout=absolute())
        # resolution-independent bounce: end resolves to (axis_max - value),
        # i.e. the right edge of whatever panel this runs on.
        s += label("msg", text="HELLO", rect=rect(0, 0, 0, 0),
                   animations=animation(
                       anim_track(StyleProp.X, 0, 0, end_inverted=True),
                       duration_ms=1500, reverse=True, repeat_count=0,
                   ))
        pad.screen_save(s)                          # F:host/s/matrix.pb
        pad.screen_load("F:host/s/matrix.pb")
```

LED-matrix specifics that matter:

- The **same widget tree renders** to the LED surface (LVGL → pixel strip), so
  every DSL widget/layout works; only the panel geometry differs. Brightness
  dims text, shapes **and images**.
- **Layout pixel-exactly with `absolute()` + `rect(x, y, w, h)`**, or use
  flex/grid with `grow_*`. Read `display_width` / `display_height` from
  `pad.board_info` rather than hard-coding a panel size.
- **Use `start_inverted` / `end_inverted` on `anim_track`** so an animation
  spans "the whole panel" on any size instead of a baked-in pixel value.
- `is_touchable == False`, so `touchy init` writes the touch-less animated setup
  screen (`build_setup_screen_touchless()`), which has **no**
  `widget_ref(id="page")` — `show_user_screen()` cannot target it. Upload and
  `screen_load()` your own screen instead.
- Diagnostics that shine on a matrix: `log_line()` (scrolls device logs on the
  panel), `fps()`, `force_render()`.
- `T:` is flash-backed on no-PSRAM boards (`info.temp_is_flash`) — throttle
  high-rate image rewrites there.
- The **simulator does not emulate a physical LED matrix**; it renders LVGL
  screens, so it is fine for layout/logic, not for panel wiring.

## Trackpad and gestures

`trackpad(id, ...)` is the multitouch surface; touches become device-side USB HID
via `Action` lists. Defaults are seeded so a bare `trackpad("pad")` behaves like
a normal touchpad (1/2/3-finger clicks, drag, 2-finger scroll); pass `[]` to
disable a gesture.

```python
from touchy_pad.api import trackpad, macro_action, mouse_move, mouse_button_down, \
    mouse_button_up, key_tap, consumer_key, VOLUME_UP, VOLUME_DOWN, hid_keys

trackpad(
    "pad",
    scroll_invert_y=True,                      # macOS-style natural scrolling
    # 1-finger swipe — OFF unless swipe_initial_distance is set
    swipe_initial_distance=60, swipe_initial_time=300,
    swipe_consecutive_distance=40, swipe_consecutive_time=200, swipe_angle=30,
    on_left_swipe=macro_action([key_tap(hid_keys.KEY_LBRACKET)]),
    # 2-finger pinch-zoom — OFF unless zoom_initial_distance is set
    zoom_initial_distance=50, zoom_consecutive_distance=25,
    on_zoom_in=macro_action([key_tap(hid_keys.KEY_EQUAL, hid_keys.CTRL)]),
    on_zoom_out=macro_action([key_tap(hid_keys.KEY_MINUS, hid_keys.CTRL)]),
    # 2-finger twist — OFF unless twist_initial_angle is set
    twist_initial_angle=15, twist_consecutive_angle=5,
    on_cw_twist=macro_action([consumer_key(VOLUME_UP)]),
    on_ccw_twist=macro_action([consumer_key(VOLUME_DOWN)]),
    # press-and-hold (drag-and-drop) — OFF unless hold_time is set
    tap_time=150, tap_distance=20, hold_time=300,
    on_hold=macro_action([mouse_button_down()]),
    on_move=macro_action([mouse_move()]),      # bare move() = live per-frame delta
    on_hold_release=macro_action([mouse_button_up()]),
)
```

Every gesture family is **opt-in via field presence** (the "master switch") and
**additive** — enabling swipes does not stop drag/scroll. Put a `log_line()` on
the page to see recognised gestures (`swipe left dx=…`, `zoom in d=…`,
`twist cw deg=…`) scroll past while you tune thresholds. The stock example is
`app/src/touchy_pad/pages/trackpad.py`.

## Rust API (async, no libusb)

The `touchy-pad` crate (`rust/touchy-pad/`, edition 2024, tokio) speaks the same
protocol over a pure-Rust `nusb` USB transport, TCP (simulator), or an optional
`serial` feature. There is **no screen DSL** in Rust: build
`touchy_pad::proto::Widget` / `Screen` prost structs directly, or author the
screen with the Python DSL and push the resulting `.pb` bytes with
`file_write_raw`. `touchy_pad::proto` is generated from the same `proto/`.

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use touchy_pad::{Touchy, ImageCache, discover};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    // Honours TOUCHY_SIM_URL (tcp://host:port); else USB, then UART bridge.
    let pad = Touchy::open().await?;

    let info = pad.client().sys_board_info_get().await?;
    println!("{} {}x{} touch={} serial={}",
             info.board_name, info.display_width, info.display_height,
             info.is_touchable, info.serial);

    // Images: PNG/JPG/GIF/WebP are auto-converted to LVGL .bin on the host.
    let png = std::fs::read("key.png")?;
    pad.file_save("R:host/images/key.png", &png).await?;

    // Content-addressed cache: upload once, repaint by slot swap.
    let pad = Arc::new(pad);
    let cache = ImageCache::new(pad.clone());
    let path = cache.set_cached_image(&png).await?;          // T:host/icache/<hash>.bin
    pad.set_image_button_slot("key_0", false, &path).await?; // repaint in place

    // Events: one consumer, a tokio mpsc stream of LvEvent.
    let mut rx = pad.events().await.expect("events() is consumed once");
    while let Some(evt) = rx.recv().await {
        println!("{evt:?}");
    }
    Ok(())
}
```

- `Touchy`: `open()`, `from_transport(Arc<dyn Transport>)`, `client()`,
  `events()`, `file_save(path, &[u8]) -> path`, `file_write_raw`,
  `screen_save(path, &Screen)`, `user_screen_save(name, &Widget)`,
  `widget_save(path, &Widget)`, `show_user_screen(name)`, `screen_load(path)`,
  `set_image_button_slot(id, pressed, path)`, `close()`.
- `Client` (via `pad.client()`): `sys_board_info_get`, `screen_wake`,
  `run_actions(Vec<Action>)`, `set_preferences`, `get_preferences`,
  `set_backlight_level`, `screen_sleep_timeout`, `set_min_log_level`,
  `file_open_write`/`file_write`/`file_close`, `event_consume`, `poll`.
- `discover()` returns `Vec<DiscoveredDevice>` (USB **and** a sim entry when
  `TOUCHY_SIM_URL` is set); `dev.describe()` / `dev.open()` → `Transport`.
- `ImageCache::new(Arc<Touchy>)` / `with_max_dim(pad, Some(px))`; `images::to_lvgl_bin` +
  `normalize_for_device` are the shared normaliser.
- `TouchyError` variants: `DeviceNotFound`, `Usb`, `Framing`, `Device{code,name}`,
  `Timeout`, `IncompatibleFirmware`. Note `Touchy::open()` requires the device's
  `protocol_version` to **equal** the crate's, unlike Python's minimum check.
- Path constants mirror Python: `touchy_pad::SCREENS_DIR`,
  `DEFAULT_SCREEN_PATH`, `USER_SCREENS_DIR`, `TEMP_DRIVE`.
- Build/test with `just rust-test`, `just rust-lint`, `just rust-doc`,
  `just rust-run -- <demo|info|listen>`.

## Developing without hardware (simulator)

The Python package ships a device simulator that implements the **same wire
protocol** (including framing) over TCP, so the exact same host code runs against
it:

```sh
touchy --sim-headless board-info        # no Qt; script/CI friendly
touchy --sim-gui screen demo            # in-process sim + Qt window
touchy simulator --headless --port 8935 # long-lived server (also serves plaintext HTTP on 8083)
touchy --sim-remote 127.0.0.1:8935      # talk to that server

export TOUCHY_SIM_URL=tcp://127.0.0.1:8935   # any consumer (Python *and* Rust) picks it up
```

In-process, for tests and host apps:

```python
from touchy_pad.api import create_sim_device, destroy_sim_device, touchy_open

create_sim_device()                 # registers a sim in this process
with touchy_open() as pad:          # no hardware needed; real API, real framing
    pad.screen_save(my_screen)
    pad.screen_load("F:host/s/my_screen.pb")
destroy_sim_device()
```

Simulator fidelity to keep in mind: it implements the documented
`set_properties` subset (`x`/`y`/`w`/`h`/`bg_color`/`text`), has **no**
backlight/auto-off, **no** LVGL refresh-latency model, and **no**
filesystem-handle/`IO_ERROR` model. It does not emulate a physical LED matrix.

## Drive a panel from any language (HTTP / HTTPS + JSON)

A WiFi-provisioned pad accepts the same commands on one endpoint — no protobuf
tooling required, because the body may be canonical protobuf-JSON:

```sh
touchy pref wifi-set-ssid MyNetwork && touchy pref wifi-set-psk hunter2
touchy pref provision-mtls          # self-signed CA + device/client certs, over USB

curl -s -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"setProperties":{"props":[{"widgetId":"welcome","propertyName":"text","stringValue":"hi"}]}}' \
  http://192.168.1.42/touchy/api/v1/command
bin/set-property.sh 192.168.1.42 welcome "You got an email"
```

- `POST /touchy/api/v1/command`; `Content-Type: application/protobuf` (default)
  or `application/json`; the body is a **bare** message (HTTP delimits it — no
  MAGIC/LEN/CRC8). The response mirrors the request encoding.
- JSON supports `setProperties`, `sysBoardInfoGet`, `screenWake`,
  `getPreferences`, `sysRebootBootloader`, `eventConsume`; `setPreferences` /
  `runActions` are protobuf-only, and an unknown key returns HTTP 400.
- Events are polled: POST `eventConsume` in a loop (same as over USB).
- From Python, use the normal API: `touchy_open(url="http://host[:port]")`, or
  set `TOUCHY_URL`. `https://` auto-loads the mTLS credentials saved by
  `touchy pref provision-mtls` (client cert required — that *is* the auth).

## CLI cheat sheet

```sh
touchy board-info                       # name, resolution, RAM/flash, touch?
touchy init                             # provision chrome + trackpad page
touchy update                           # install/upgrade firmware
touchy screen load F:host/s/home.pb     # activate a screen
touchy screen wake                      # backlight on (cancel auto-sleep)
touchy screen demo                      # upload the demo page set
touchy touchpad image URL | touchpad gif
touchy file-save PATH FILE  |  file-delete PATH  |  file-reset
touchy events                           # stream device events (Ctrl-C)
touchy property set WIDGET_ID PROPERTY VALUE [--int]
touchy pref backlight-level 0-100 | log-level | boot-delay | backlight-timeout
touchy pref from-template NAME | json-get | json-set | wifi-set-ssid | wifi-set-psk | provision-mtls
touchy simulator [--headless] [--port N]
```

## Gotchas that bite

- **Paths are drive-prefixed.** `F:` flash, `R:` PSRAM ramdisk, `T:` transient.
  A bare `host/...` is wrong. Screens `F:host/s/`, pages `F:host/uscr/`,
  standalone widgets `F:host/w/`.
- **Wire versions are validated on load, and a mismatch deletes the file.** After
  a firmware update that bumps `Widget.Version`, re-upload your screens
  (`pad.screen_save(...)` / `user_screen_save(...)`).
- **The root `Widget` carries the version** (there is no `Screen.Version`). The
  DSL stamps it; for raw protobuf set
  `msg.active.version = protobuf.Widget.Version.CURRENT`.
- **`#` is the LVGL recolor delimiter** and this LVGL's `##` escape is dead code:
  with `recolor=True` a literal `#` in the text is swallowed — strip it host-side.
- **Scrolling labels only animate when their box is fixed and narrower than the
  text.** Default scroll speed is 40 px/s; set `scroll_speed_px_s` (10…10000) or
  `scroll_duration_ms` (mutually exclusive), or re-time live with
  `build_property_override(id, "anim_duration", ms)`.
- **Content-size by default**: forgetting `grow_x`/`grow_y` is why a button looks
  tiny. Grid children centre unless they grow.
- **Keep event callbacks short** — they run on the poller thread and block
  protocol polling; multiple callbacks per code run in registration order.
- **Windows has no libusb**: USB discovery must degrade to a clear error
  (`NoBackendError`), not a traceback. On Linux you need the udev rule
  (`bin/install-rules.sh`, see `docs/udev.md`).
- **A long-lived process may not see a re-plugged pad** (libusb caches its device
  list per context). Re-open (`touchy_open()`) after re-plugging instead of
  reusing a stale handle; `just usb-diag` diagnoses it.
- **The device is a renderer.** It has no internet access and no knowledge of
  your data — the host does the thinking, the device draws and reports touches.
- **Generated code is generated**: `app/src/touchy_pad/_proto/*`,
  `firmware/main/proto/*`, `proto/default_screen.json` — regenerate with
  `just build-proto`, never hand-edit.
- **Working inside this repo?** Drive everything through `just`
  (`just app-test`, `just app-lint`, `just build-proto`, `just firmware-build`,
  `just rust-test`) — never raw `idf.py`/`poetry`/`protoc`. Never commit or push;
  hand the change to the human.

## Typical app patterns

| Want to build | Building blocks |
|---|---|
| **Status / info panel** | `Screen` + `grid`/`col` + `label`; refresh with `set_properties([...])` from a loop (`build_property_override`), which also keeps the backlight awake. |
| **StreamDeck-style key grid** | `grid` + `image_button` per key (stable ids) + `ImageCache` + `pad.set_image_button_slot(id, pressed, path)`; `on_press`/`on_release` → `host_action` or `macro_action`. |
| **Remote signage / ticker** | `label(long_mode=LongMode.LONG_MODE_SCROLL_CIRCULAR, recolor=True, scroll_speed_px_s=…)` plus a host loop pushing `text` overrides; or the HTTP/JSON endpoint from any language. |
| **LED art / hanging column** | LED board + `touchy pref from-template led-96x8-chain`, `absolute()` + `rect`, `anim_track(..., end_inverted=True)` for size-independent motion, `ImageSource`/`set_properties` for frames. |
| **Macro pad / touchpad** | `trackpad(...)` with gesture `Action` lists + `macros.*`; works with no host app attached. |
| **StreamController / OpenDeck** | `touchy_pad.touchydeck.TouchyDeck` shim (call `install()` explicitly) or the `touchy-opendeck` plugin. |
